answer: The pooled gene expression (log2(TPM+1), batch-corrected) distribution across all cell lines is positively (right) skewed, with Fisher–Pearson sample skewness G1 = 0.690 (adjusted, pandas .skew()/scipy bias=False; unadjusted g1 = 0.689708, identical to 6 decimals at N = 32,017,874). Interpretation: moderately positive right skew — the mean (2.612) exceeds the median (2.342), with a long right tail of highly expressed genes (Q75 = 4.491, max = 18.437) balanced by a left shoulder of low/undetectable expression (Q25 = 0.079, min = −2.623, the latter a batch-correction artifact). Supporting stats: N = 32,017,874 values from 1,673 cell lines × 19,138 protein-coding genes; all 1,673 row IDs exactly match ModelID in Model.csv (of 2,105 models); zero NaN cells, so no imputation was needed. Sensitivity note: restricting to non-negative values only (N = 28,469,302) gives G1 = 0.561 — same sign and moderate-magnitude interpretation.
